claude.sample_unit: abdominopelvic planning CT images (165 training, 15 validation)

links.outcome: Contouring time and DSC for radiation oncologists with versus without AI auto-segmentation
links.effect: Median contouring time 82 min without vs 51 min with auto-segmentation; mean DSC 0.76 vs 0.82; HD 25.11 vs 24.40 mm; smaller SDs suggest reduced heterogeneity.
links.quote: The median times for contouring all OAR/CTVs without auto-segmentation and with auto-segmentation were 82 min (range, 66–101 min) and 51 min (range, 31–78 min), respectively.

links.outcome: Generalizability across sites and scanners; external validation
links.effect: Single-institution data with two CT scanners; no external validation; small validation set (15) acknowledged as limitation.
links.quote: Further external validation using data from other institutions is needed and will be planned as an additional project in the future.

unlisted_practices: Turing test and physician preference/satisfaction evaluation of AI-generated contours
Geometric overlap metrics (DSC, HD) are poorly correlated with clinical acceptability, so multi-domain evaluation is needed

models_evaluated: U-Net with EfficientNet-B0 deep learning auto-segmentation model

links.outcome: contouring time with versus without AI
links.effect: Median contouring time was 82 min (66–101) without auto-segmentation vs 51 min (31–78) with auto-segmentation.
links.quote: The median times for contouring all OAR/CTVs without auto-segmentation and with auto-segmentation were 82 min (range, 66–101 min) and 51 min (range, 31–78 min), respectively.

links.outcome: clinician review of AI contour errors
links.effect: Blinded participants accepted 66% of auto-segmented contours as-is and required minor-error correction for 34%.
links.quote: For the auto-segmented contours, which were blinded, the participants answered that they would accept them as they are for 66% and that they would require them to be corrected since they have minor errors for 34%.

links.outcome: conflict between AI target volume contours and institutional routine practice
links.effect: 9 of 10 radiation oncologists reported auto-segmented CTVs differed from their institution's routine practice, though OARs were similar
links.quote: All participants, except one, answered that the CTVs were different from those of their institution, but that the OARs were similar.
